correctness.rationale: The exact two-count Markov transition law follows by enumerating all V-trimer paths. The gamma-ratio integrates the conditional drift exactly; its increments have bounded predictable quadratic variation of order \(N^{1/3}\). For nonzero relative imbalance, the martingale has deterministic leading order \(N^{2/3}\) and terminal boundary inversion gives the \(\lvert\delta\rvert^{3/2}\) law. For square-root imbalance, a stopped martingale CLT above \(N^{1/2}\) plus negligible lower-stage variation yields a unit-variance shifted normal; the barrier gives the \(N^{1/4}\) Gaussian-power limit. Independently enumerated physical terminal distributions agree with exact rational recursions on nine graphs, conditional moments and the gamma identity are checked, and seeded simulations corroborate but are not used as an infinite proof. A cutoff at three free vertices is accounted for by the continuous Gaussian no-atom property.

originality.rationale: Available references, five semantic research-record queries, targeted primary-literature searches, and the accessible claim history were compared by statement and implication. The only fully read close trimer primary article covers planar continuum adsorption and does not determine the terminal chain on complete bipartite graphs. Abstracts and full-text extracts on lattice RSA, random greedy sparse graph adsorption, and general hypergraph matching do not supply the explicit critical exponent or terminal distribution. Missing full text remains a stated risk, not a false claim of exhaustive novelty.
residual_risks: An equivalent deletion-urn process could have been solved under different terminology; broad searches do not eliminate this possibility.
Full text of de Oliveira–Tomé (1994) and Pippenger (1989) was unavailable; the disclosed assessment does not assert full-text NOT_COVERING.
Complete arXiv manuscripts for the two general hypergraph-matching papers were not read; the stated theorem hypotheses and conclusions were compared from accessible material.
Unindexed reports and tables may contain a special case despite negative search results.

value.rationale: Random greedy packing of the natural bent three-site adsorbate on complete bipartite substrates reveals a sharp fluctuation transition: a fixed class imbalance leaves a strictly positive kinetic vacancy fraction even where perfect packings exist, while balance produces a non-Gaussian quarter-root-scale residual. The closed exponent and distribution provide quantitative kinetic benchmarks not implied by generic hypergraph near-perfect matching existence statements.
